title: Self-Assessment Report 2025/26
summary: Delcorn's annual self-assessment of apprenticeship quality for 2025/26 against the Ofsted report-card framework, with judgements, strengths, areas for improvement and supporting data.
author: P005

version_history.change: Data tables and observation evidence added
Leadership & governance section drafted; learner voice triangulated
Revised after executive review; for Board approval 10 Dec 2026

blocks.p: This self-assessment report (SAR) evaluates the quality of Delcorn's apprenticeship provision for the academic year 2025/26 (1 August 2025 – 31 July 2026). It has been written against the Ofsted report-card framework used at our inspection in February 2026 and follows the same five evaluation areas: **achievement**, **curriculum and teaching**, **participation and development**, **inclusion**, and **leadership and governance**.

Delcorn delivers apprenticeships from Level 3 to Level 7 through five academies (AI, Data, Digital, Leadership and People) to large employers across England. All delivery is remote: skills coaches provide 1:1 coaching and 12-weekly tripartite progress reviews, academies run live online workshops, and apprentices record evidence and off-the-job (OTJ) training in Aptiva. At 5 November 2026 there were {{fact:active_learners}} apprentices on programme with {{fact:active_employers}} active employer partners.

The SAR draws on Aptiva and ILR data, the coaching observation programme, learner and employer voice, EPA results, internal funding audits, safeguarding records (aggregate only) and the findings of the February 2026 inspection. Every judgement below cites its evidence; where evidence is incomplete we say so.

Strong standard in all evaluation areas

blocks.p: **Judgement: Strong standard.** The overall achievement rate rose by 14 percentage points, from {{fact:achievement_rate_2425}} in 2024/25 to {{fact:achievement_rate_2526}} in 2025/26, placing Delcorn well above the most recent national rate for apprenticeships. Of {{fact:leavers_2526}} leavers, {{fact:withdrawals_2526}} withdrew. The most common withdrawal reason remains '{{fact:top_withdrawal_reason}}', which is largely outside our control but is mitigated by our transfer-to-new-employer process.

blocks.p: Achievement is strongest in the Data Academy and weakest in the People Academy and Digital Academy, both of which are smaller and were affected by coach turnover in the first half of the year. The EPA grade profile is positive: the first-attempt pass rate for 2025/26 was {{fact:qual_epa_first_attempt_2526}}, and around one in four apprentices achieved a Distinction.

bullets: Sustained improvement in achievement across all five academies, driven by the at-risk learner process introduced in September 2025.
High proportion of Merit and Distinction grades, particularly on Data Analyst (DA4) and Operations Manager (OM5).
Gateway readiness checks mean very few apprentices fail EPA at first attempt.
Close the achievement gap in the People and Digital academies (QIP ref QIP-01).
Reduce early withdrawals in the first 90 days by strengthening initial assessment and employer commitment to OTJ (QIP-02).
Improve timeliness: a minority of apprentices pass their planned end date before reaching gateway.

blocks.p: **Judgement: Strong standard.** Curricula are ambitious, current and planned with employers, particularly in the AI Academy, where content is reviewed each term against developments in generative AI and regulation. Coaches are industry experts who use real employer data and projects. During 2025/26 we completed {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coach_observations WHERE obs_date BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2026-07-31'}} observations of coaching, workshops and reviews; {{fact:qual_obs_strong_pct_2526}} were graded Strong and {{sql:SELECT 1.0*SUM(grade IN ('Strong','Secure'))/COUNT(*) FROM coach_observations WHERE obs_date BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2026-07-31'|pct}} Strong or Secure.

table.sql: SELECT grade AS Grade, COUNT(*) AS Observations, printf('%.1f%%', 100.0*COUNT(*)/(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coach_observations WHERE obs_date BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2026-07-31')) AS Share FROM coach_observations WHERE obs_date BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE grade WHEN 'Strong' THEN 1 WHEN 'Secure' THEN 2 WHEN 'Developing' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
table.caption: Table 5 – Observation grades, 2025/26

bullets: Skilful questioning and personalised targets were the most frequently recorded strengths in observations.
Strong links between KSBs and workplace tasks; apprentices apply learning quickly (e.g. automating reports, building dashboards).
Live workshops are rated highly by learners and are recorded for those who cannot attend.
Targets set in progress reviews are not always specific or measurable (QIP-04).
Coaches do not consistently use Aptiva evidence during sessions to check and extend learning (QIP-05).
More able apprentices are not always stretched towards Distinction criteria early enough.

blocks.p: **Judgement: Strong standard.** Apprentices value their programmes: the 12-month learner NPS is {{fact:learner_nps_12m}}. Personal development, careers guidance and wellbeing support are well integrated into reviews. Attendance at live workshops averaged 81% across the year.

table.sql: SELECT survey AS Survey, COUNT(*) AS Responses, SUM(nps_category='Promoter') AS Promoters, SUM(nps_category='Detractor') AS Detractors, printf('%+d', ROUND(100.0*SUM(nps_category='Promoter')/COUNT(*) - 100.0*SUM(nps_category='Detractor')/COUNT(*))) AS NPS, printf('%.2f', AVG(coach_rating)) AS "Coach rating (1-5)", printf('%.2f', AVG(workshop_rating)) AS "Workshop rating (1-5)" FROM learner_feedback WHERE response_date > '2025-11-05' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
table.caption: Table 7 – Learner voice by survey, last 12 months

blocks.p: The most common negative theme in learner comments is lack of time for OTJ training alongside work; a small number of apprentices report that their manager does not protect learning time. At 5 November 2026, {{fact:qual_otj_behind_active}} active apprentices were more than 20% behind their expected OTJ hours.

bullets: Work with employers to secure protected OTJ time, especially for shift-based roles (QIP-06).
Reduce rescheduled progress reviews; at 5 November 2026, {{fact:overdue_reviews}} reviews were overdue (QIP-07).

blocks.p: **Judgement: Strong standard.** Apprentices with learning difficulties or disabilities (LLDD) achieve in line with their peers. Additional learning support (ALS) is identified at initial assessment and reviewed every 12 weeks. Safeguarding arrangements are effective: {{fact:sg_concerns_2526}} concerns were raised in 2025/26 and all were triaged by the DSL team on the day they were raised. The most common category was {{fact:sg_top_category}}.

table.sql: SELECT CASE lldd WHEN 1 THEN 'LLDD declared' ELSE 'No LLDD declared' END AS Group_, COUNT(*) AS Leavers, printf('%.1f%%', 100.0*SUM(status='Completed')/COUNT(*)) AS "Achievement rate" FROM learners WHERE status IN ('Completed','Withdrawn') AND actual_end_date BETWEEN '2025-08-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY 1
table.caption: Table 8 – Achievement by LLDD status, 2025/26

bullets: Embed Prevent and British values discussion more naturally in coaching, rather than as a checklist item (QIP-08).
Increase uptake of Functional Skills support by apprentices who are exempt but would benefit.

blocks.p: **Judgement: Strong standard.** Leaders have a clear, ambitious vision and act on accurate data. The Quality Committee meets six times a year; the Meridian Education Group board receives a quality and safeguarding report each term. Funding compliance is robust: internal OTJ sampling found no material errors, although evidence quality varies (see the Funding Compliance Audit Q1 2026/27).

bullets: Strong governance oversight of safeguarding, with an independent safeguarding governor appointed in January 2026.
Staff development is well planned; all coaches complete at least 30 hours of CPD per year.
Area for improvement: the QIP needs sharper, measurable success criteria and monthly RAG review (QIP-10).

blocks.p: Areas for improvement are carried into the Quality Improvement Plan 2026/27, which is reviewed monthly by the Quality Manager and each meeting of the Quality Committee.

title: Ofsted Inspection Report Summary — February 2026
summary: Delcorn's internal summary of the February 2026 Ofsted inspection outcome: Strong standard in all evaluation areas, key findings and recommendations.
author: P005

version_history.change: First draft after publication of report

kv: Lead inspector plus four Ofsted inspectors (remote and on-site with employers)
Dr Siân Llewellyn, Director of Quality & Compliance

bullets: Inspectors judged curricula to be ambitious and highly relevant to employers' needs, particularly in AI and data, where coaches 'bring current industry practice into every session'.
Apprentices develop substantial new knowledge, skills and behaviours and apply them at work quickly; employers gave many examples of productivity gains.
Achievement has improved markedly and is now high; the proportion of high grades at EPA is above that of similar providers.
Progress reviews are thorough and involve employers well, although targets are sometimes too broad.
Safeguarding arrangements are effective. Apprentices feel safe, know how to report concerns and understand the risks of radicalisation and online harms relevant to their sectors.
Leaders and governors have an accurate view of strengths and weaknesses; self-assessment closely matched inspection findings.

blocks.h1: What Delcorn should do to improve

numbered: Ensure coaches set precise, measurable targets in every progress review so that apprentices know exactly what they need to do next.
Work with a minority of employers to make sure apprentices receive their full entitlement to off-the-job training.
Ensure that the most able apprentices are challenged early to achieve the highest grades.
Strengthen the way coaches revisit Prevent and British values so that apprentices' understanding is deepened over time.

blocks.callout: All four recommendations were incorporated into the Quality Improvement Plan 2026/27 (QIP-04, QIP-06, QIP-05 and QIP-08).
blocks.title: Follow-up

bullets: The Inspection Readiness Evidence Map made it easy to retrieve evidence during the call; keep it current monthly.
Inspectors sampled 46 apprentices; having review records signed by all parties was essential.
Employer interviews were the most influential evidence for curriculum judgements — maintain a bank of willing employer contacts.

title: Observation of Coaching Framework
summary: How Delcorn observes coaching, workshops, progress reviews and Functional Skills lessons, with grade descriptors Strong, Secure, Developing and Requires improvement.
author: P021

version_history.change: New developmental framework replacing graded lesson observations
Aligned to report-card framework; re-observation timescales tightened

blocks.p: Observation is how we assure and improve the quality of teaching, coaching and assessment. It is developmental: its purpose is to help every coach and tutor improve, and to give leaders an accurate picture of quality to inform the SAR. Grades are recorded against the descriptors below and are never used in isolation for performance management.

bullets: Every skills coach and Functional Skills tutor is formally observed **at least once each academic year**.
New coaches are observed **within their first 3 months**, before their probation review.
Any session graded Requires improvement is followed by a support plan and a **re-observation within 6 weeks**.
Sessions graded Developing are re-observed within one term.
Session types: 1:1 coaching, progress review, group workshop, Functional Skills lesson and Gateway preparation.

blocks.p: Observations are carried out by the Quality Manager (Hannah Price), the Director of Quality & Compliance, the Head of Delivery and delivery managers, all of whom complete annual standardisation. Ten per cent of observations are jointly observed to moderate judgements.

rows: Learning is highly effective. The coach skilfully sequences content, uses questioning to deepen thinking, links every activity to KSBs and the workplace, and stretches the apprentice towards higher grades. Wellbeing, Prevent and British values are woven in naturally. Targets are precise and owned by the apprentice.
Learning is effective. The session is well planned and relevant, the apprentice makes clear progress and targets are mostly specific. Minor improvements would increase impact.
Some learning takes place, but planning, questioning, use of evidence or target setting are inconsistent. The apprentice's progress is not always checked. A development plan is agreed.

Learning is not effective or the apprentice is not making sufficient progress. Significant weaknesses exist in planning, checking understanding, compliance (e.g. OTJ, safeguarding) or employer involvement. A support plan and re-observation within 6 weeks are mandatory.
table.caption: Table 1 – Grade descriptors

numbered: Observer agrees the session with the coach at least 5 working days in advance (unannounced 'drop-ins' are used only for follow-up).
Observer joins the Teams session with camera off after introduction; learner consent is confirmed at the start.
Observer records evidence against the five focus areas: planning; questioning and checking learning; KSB and workplace links; personal development and safeguarding; target setting.
Verbal feedback within 2 working days; written record in the observation log within 5 working days.
Coach and observer agree one strength and one development area, recorded in the log.
Follow-up actions are tracked by the Quality Manager and reported to the Quality Committee.

blocks.p: Aggregate results are reported termly by academy and session type and summarised annually in the Observation Summary Report. Individual records are confidential to the coach, their manager and the Quality team.

title: Funding Compliance Audit — OTJ Sampling Q1 2026/27
summary: Internal sample audit of off-the-job training evidence for August–October 2026, with findings, risk ratings and actions.
author: P022

version_history.change: Draft findings to Director of Quality

blocks.p: This audit tested whether off-the-job (OTJ) training recorded in Aptiva for apprentices on programme between 1 August and 31 October 2026 is planned, evidenced and compliant with the Department for Education apprenticeship funding rules. A risk-weighted sample of 60 apprentices was drawn across all five academies, over-sampling learners flagged in Aptiva as more than 20% behind their expected OTJ hours.

kv: Daniel Evans, Compliance & Funding Assurance Lead

blocks.callout: **Reasonable assurance.** No ineligible funding claims were identified. OTJ planning is compliant in all sampled cases, but evidence quality and the escalation of learners behind plan need improvement.
blocks.title: Opinion

7/20 had no catch-up plan in the latest review

OTJ hours recorded during annual leave or BIL dates

blocks.p: Compared with the Q4 2025/26 audit, vague OTJ entries fell from 24% to 18% of the sample, but the proportion of behind-plan learners without a catch-up plan rose from 25% to 35%. QIP-06 is therefore rated Red.

title: Complaints Policy
summary: How apprentices, employers and others can complain, the three stages, timescales and escalation to the Department for Education.
author: P021

blocks.p: Delcorn welcomes feedback and treats complaints as an opportunity to improve. This policy explains how apprentices, employers, parents or carers and members of the public can raise a complaint and what they can expect from us.
Most concerns can be resolved quickly by speaking to your skills coach, delivery manager or account manager. We encourage this first, but you may go straight to a formal complaint if you prefer.

rows: Quality Manager assigns an investigating manager
Acknowledged within 3 working days; full response within 15 working days
Request within 10 working days of Stage 1 response; response within 15 working days
Department for Education apprenticeship service complaints team
table.caption: Table 1 – Complaint stages

blocks.p: Complaints can be made by emailing complaints@delcorn.co.uk, using the form in Aptiva, or by telephone on 020 7946 0100. Please include your name, programme, a description of the issue and what outcome you are seeking.

If a complaint raises a safeguarding concern it is passed immediately to the Designated Safeguarding Lead and handled under the Safeguarding & Prevent Policy. Staff concerns about wrongdoing are handled under the Whistleblowing Policy.

bullets: All formal complaints are logged by the Quality team, including outcome and lessons learned.
Themes are reported to every Quality Committee and summarised in the SAR.
Complainants will not be treated less favourably for raising a complaint.

title: Safeguarding & Prevent Policy 2026/27
summary: Delcorn's safeguarding and Prevent duty policy for 2026/27: roles, how to report a concern, Prevent risk assessment, online safety, record keeping and key contacts.
author: P010

version_history.change: Annual review; KCSIE and Prevent duty guidance updates
Online safety and AI-generated content risks added
Annual review; reporting via Aptiva Safeguarding form; Meridian group governor role

blocks.p: Delcorn is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of every apprentice, including adults at risk and the small number of apprentices aged 16–18. Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility. All staff, contractors and volunteers must act on any concern, however small, and must never promise confidentiality to a learner.

This policy meets our duties under the Children Act 1989 and 2004, the Care Act 2014, Keeping Children Safe in Education, the Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015 (Prevent duty) and the Department for Education funding rules. It applies to remote and in-person contact, including Teams sessions, email, Aptiva messages and visits to employers.

rows: Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and Prevent Lead
Strategic lead; decides on referrals to external agencies; Channel and local authority Prevent liaison; reports to the Board
Deputy DSL and Learner Support Lead
Case management; acts as DSL in Grace's absence; coordinates wellbeing and additional learning support
First-line support to coaches; cover rota
Nominated Meridian Education Group board member
Recognise, respond, report and record; complete annual training
table.caption: Table 1 – Safeguarding roles

bullets: Mental health concerns, including anxiety, low mood, self-harm or suicidal thoughts.
Domestic abuse, coercive control, honour-based abuse and forced marriage.
Financial hardship, housing insecurity or homelessness.
Bullying, harassment or discrimination in the workplace.
Online harms: sextortion, scams, grooming, misuse of AI-generated images.
Substance misuse.
Radicalisation or extremist views (Prevent).
Neglect, exploitation (including modern slavery) and abuse by a person in a position of trust.

blocks.callout: If someone is in immediate danger, call **999** first, then inform the DSL. Otherwise report the **same working day** — and immediately if you believe there is a risk of harm.
blocks.title: Golden rule

numbered: **Listen** calmly; do not ask leading questions or investigate.
**Do not promise confidentiality** — explain that you will need to share the concern with the safeguarding team.
**Report** to the safeguarding team by phoning the safeguarding line on 020 7946 0199 (08:00–18:00, Mon–Fri) or calling the DSL or Deputy DSL directly.
**Record** the concern on the Aptiva Safeguarding form within 24 hours, using the learner's words where possible. Use the learner ID; do not include details in email or Teams.
The DSL team triages the concern **on the day it is received**, assigns a risk level (High, Medium or Low) and a case ID, and confirms next steps to the reporter.
High-risk cases are reviewed by the DSL within 24 hours; the DSL decides whether to refer to an external agency (police, local authority, adult social care, Prevent team, GP or EAP).

blocks.p: Outside office hours, staff should contact emergency services if required and email safeguarding@delcorn.co.uk, which is monitored by the on-call DSL until 21:00 on weekdays and 10:00–16:00 at weekends.

Delcorn has a duty to have due regard to the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism. We do this by training staff, promoting fundamental British values (democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance), managing online risks and referring concerns appropriately. Prevent concerns follow the same reporting route; only the DSL makes a Prevent referral to the local authority or police.

rows: Remote delivery limits observation of behaviour
Coach training; camera-on reviews; wellbeing check in every review
Online safety module at induction; termly content in workshops
table.caption: Table 2 – Prevent risk assessment 2026/27 (full assessment held in the Prevent Risk Assessment & Action Plan)

blocks.p: Since March 2025, {{fact:sg_prevent_cases}} concerns have been recorded under the Prevent category; all were assessed by the DSL and, where appropriate, discussed with the local authority Prevent team.

bullets: All sessions use Delcorn Microsoft Teams accounts; never personal messaging apps or social media.
Recordings of 1:1 sessions are only made with consent and stored in Aptiva.
Coaches must not share personal contact details with apprentices.
Apprentices complete the online safety module, including scams, sextortion and AI-generated content, in their first month.
Web filtering and monitoring apply to Delcorn devices; concerns are routed to the DSL.
Safeguarding records are kept in Aptiva Safeguarding and the restricted **Case Management** library, accessible only to the DSL team.
Records are labelled **Highly Confidential**; they must not be copied to other sites, emails, Teams chats or AI tools.
Reports and dashboards use aggregate data only — no learner names.
Information is shared with external agencies on a need-to-know basis under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, recorded with the reason.
Records are retained for 6 years after the apprentice leaves, or longer if a case is ongoing.

blocks.p: Allegations that a member of staff may have harmed a learner are reported directly to the DSL (or to the COO if the allegation concerns the DSL). The Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) is contacted within one working day where the learner is under 18 or an adult at risk.

bullets: All staff: safeguarding and Prevent induction in the first week; annual refresher by 31 August.
Coaches: additional annual briefing on recognising and responding to disclosures.
DSL team: Level 3 DSL training every 2 years and termly supervision.

title: Learner Support & Additional Learning Support Procedure
summary: How Delcorn identifies, plans, delivers and reviews additional learning support and reasonable adjustments for apprentices.
author: P023

version_history.change: Annual review; ALS funding evidence clarified

blocks.p: This procedure makes sure every apprentice who needs extra help to succeed — because of a learning difficulty, disability, health condition or other barrier — receives timely, effective support, and that ALS funding is claimed only where support is planned, delivered and evidenced.

bullets: Self-declaration at enrolment (LLDD question) and the initial assessment screening tool.
Coach observation or disclosure during reviews.
Functional Skills diagnostics.
Employer information (with consent).

numbered: Coach or enrolment team refers via the Aptiva Learner Support form within 5 working days of the need being identified.
Learner Support Lead (Megan Taylor) contacts the apprentice within 5 working days to discuss needs.
An ALS plan is agreed and signed by the apprentice, coach and Learner Support Lead within 20 working days of referral.
Support is delivered (e.g. specialist tutor sessions, assistive technology, extra time, recorded workshops with captions).
Impact is reviewed at every 12-weekly progress review and the plan updated.
Reasonable adjustments for EPA are requested from the EPAO at least 8 weeks before gateway.

blocks.p: ALS funding is claimed monthly only where there is a signed plan and evidence of support delivered in the month. The Compliance & Funding Assurance Lead samples ALS evidence each quarter.
If support needs relate to mental health, safety or wellbeing, the Learner Support Lead considers whether a safeguarding concern should be raised under the Safeguarding & Prevent Policy.
Information about disabilities and health is special category data. It is shared only with those who need it to provide support, with the apprentice's consent.

title: Mental Health & Wellbeing Signposting Guide for Learners
summary: Learner-facing guide to looking after your wellbeing, getting help from Delcorn and external support services.
author: P023

version_history.change: Helpline numbers checked; added financial support

blocks.h1: Looking after yourself during your apprenticeship

blocks.p: Balancing work, study and life can be hard. It's normal to have difficult times — and it's always okay to ask for help. Your skills coach checks in on your wellbeing at every review, but you don't have to wait for a review to talk to us.

bullets: Talk to your skills coach — they can help with workload, OTJ time and adjustments.
Contact the safeguarding team: safeguarding@delcorn.co.uk or 020 7946 0199 (08:00–18:00, Monday to Friday).
Ask for additional learning support if you have a learning difficulty, disability or health condition.
Request a break in learning if you need time away from your apprenticeship.

blocks.callout: If you are in immediate danger or have seriously harmed yourself, call **999** or go to A&E.
blocks.title: In an emergency

bullets: Block out OTJ time in your calendar and agree it with your manager.
Take breaks away from screens.
Stay connected — join the learner community in Teams.
Keep sleep, exercise and food routines where you can.

subject: Wellbeing concern – LRN21231
summary: Data coach raises a wellbeing concern to the DSL using learner ID only; DSL triages, opens case SG3016 and advises on next steps.

messages.body:
Hi Grace,

I've just finished a progress review with LRN21231 and I'm worried about them. They said they haven't been sleeping, feel like they're 'failing at everything' and became tearful when we talked about their EPA timeline. No mention of self-harm, but they did say they'd been avoiding friends and family.

I haven't promised to keep it confidential and told them I'd pass it to the safeguarding team. I'm completing the Aptiva Safeguarding form now. They're happy to be contacted on their work mobile this afternoon.

Is there anything you'd like me to do in the meantime?

Thanks,
James

Hi James,

Thank you — you've done exactly the right thing, and thank you for keeping the detail out of email. I've read your Aptiva form and logged this as case SG3016, Medium risk, with me as case lead.

I'll call the learner at 2pm today to talk through how they're feeling, agree a safety plan and encourage them to contact their GP. I'll also check whether their employer's EAP is an option.

In the meantime, please don't follow up on the disclosure yourself. If they contact you before I've spoken to them and anything suggests immediate risk, call me straight away or 999.

Could you hold off on the EPA timeline conversation for now? We'll pick that up together once I've spoken to them.

Grace

Thanks Grace, will do. I've paused the gateway prep tasks in Aptiva and moved our next session to next week.

James

Morning James,

Quick update: I spoke to the learner yesterday. A safety plan is in place, they have a GP appointment this week and they're happy for you to carry on coaching as normal. Further detail is in the case record.

Please keep your next session supportive and log a wellbeing check in the review. I'll review the case on 9 November. If you'd like a debrief, Megan has supervision slots on Thursday.

Thanks again for acting so quickly.

Grace

subject: Q1 OTJ sampling – draft findings
summary: Compliance lead shares draft OTJ audit findings; Director of Quality and Quality Manager agree escalation of behind-plan learners and QIP-06 rating.

messages.body:
Hi Siân,

Draft findings from the Q1 OTJ sample (60 learners) are below; full draft is in the Funding Audits folder.

- No ineligible claims and all training plans compliant.
- 11/60 have vague OTJ entries with no KSB link — better than Q4 (24%) but still not where we need it.
- 7 of the 20 behind-plan learners have no catch-up plan in their latest review. This is the one that worries me.
- 2 entries logged during BIL/annual leave — corrected, 9 hours in total.

I'd like to rate F3 as High and QIP-06 as Red. Are you comfortable with that before I send for management responses?

Thanks,
Daniel

Morning Daniel,

Thanks — clear and well evidenced. Yes, High for F3 and Red for QIP-06. If an auditor or inspector sampled those seven, we couldn't show we'd acted, and that's exactly the Ofsted recommendation we committed to fix.

Rachel — copying you in. Can Sam get catch-up plans in place for the seven by 14 November? Daniel will send the IDs.

Hannah, please reflect the Red in the QIP update and the SAR participation section.

Siân

Will do. I'll also add a line to the Learner Voice report — OTJ time is the top negative theme in comments, so it triangulates nicely with Daniel's findings.

Daniel, could you re-test F3 in the Q2 sample so we have evidence of impact before the Board?

Hannah

Final report now approved and saved. Re-test of F3 and F5 is in the Q2 plan (fieldwork late January). Kate has confirmed the Aptiva KSB field can be made mandatory by mid-December.

Daniel
